title: Stopping Computation for Converged Tokens in Masked Diffusion-LM Decoding
claim: A baseline recomputes every position at every step, while ours permanently locks settled positions and reuses their cached keys and values, saving compute.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels (a) Baseline / (b) Ours, top-to-bottom time axis t=1 to t=0, legend bar on top, token grids with arrows
description: A legend strip across the top defines the symbols: white boxes are masked tokens, blue boxes are decoded tokens, pale green dashed boxes are positions reused with cached KV, an orange padlock marks a locking action, and a black arrow marks step-wise compute. Below are two token grids with 11 columns and 6 rows each. The vertical axis is time, running from t=1 at the top to t=0 at the bottom. Panel (a) Baseline has a black arrow between every pair of rows in every column, so all positions are recomputed at every step. Panel (b) SureLock has the same layout, but padlocks appear as tokens become decoded. Locked columns turn pale green and lose their arrows, so the arrows thin out toward the bottom. A red footnote says locked tokens are still attended to via cached K/V. The eye goes first to the dense arrows on the left, then to the sparse arrows and pale green cells on the right.
caption: Iterative sampling by a normal sampler and SureLock. (a) Baseline consistently recomputes attention scores and FFN sublayers for every token position at every step even after the marginal tokens have become unmasked. (b) SureLock permanently stops recomputing for locked positions once these positions are locked. Via cached $K/V$, other tokens still attend to locked tokens.
abstract: Masked Diffusion Language Models generate sequences via iterative sampling that progressively unmasks tokens. However, they still recompute the attention and feed-forward blocks for every token position at every step -- even when many unmasked tokens are essentially fixed, resulting in substantial waste in compute. We propose SureLock: when the posterior at an unmasked position has stabilized across steps (our sure condition), we lock that position -- thereafter skipping its query projection and feed-forward sublayers -- while caching its attention keys and values so other positions can continue to attend to it. This reduces the dominant per-iteration computational cost from $O(N^2d)$ to $O(MNd)$ where $N$ is the sequence length, $M$ is the number of unlocked token positions, and $d$ is the model dimension. In practice, $M$ decreases as the iteration progresses, yielding substantial savings. On LLaDA-8B, SureLock reduces algorithmic FLOPs by 30--50% relative to the same sampler without locking, while maintaining comparable generation quality. We also provide a theoretical analysis to justify the design rationale of SureLock: monitoring only the local KL at the lock step suffices to bound the deviation in final token probabilities. Our project page is available at https://daioba.github.io/surelock .
